messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTO-PAGE fired to @pagerduty for policy 'gpu_memory_pressure_high' (severity: P1). Observed sustained CUDA OOM on pool 'inference-gpu-eu-west-2a' (>7/10 servers).

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident #PD-84231 created and paged to schedule: eng-oncall. Incident URL: https://pd.example/incidents/PD-84231

Alex M: acked via PD. I'm on it, looking at metrics and recent deploys.

Maya S: seeing similar alerts in datadog: nvml.memory.used spikes then kernel alloc fails. 

Jamal R: logs from node gpu-12 show repeated: 
```
E tensorflow: 2026-03-12 03:21:09.123456 CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
E runtime: kernel launch failed: invalid device memory state
```

Nina (oncall): any customer impact yet? Alerts show elevated 5xx for /v1/generate on eu region.

Alex M: yes, 5xx from this pool only, fallback to cpu-inference is happening but latency skyrockets (~2s -> ~8s). Not widespread but multiple paid customers affected.

Li: grabbing pool allocations: `kubectl get pods -n redwood-inference -l pool=inference-gpu-eu-west-2a -o wide` shows a lot of pods in CrashLoopBackOff.

Chris P: running `nvidia-smi` on gpu-12: 
```
GPU 0: 3090 Ti, 99% mem, Processes: 12
GPU 1: 3090 Ti, 98% mem, Processes: 11
GPU 2: 3090 Ti, 100% mem, Processes: 14 (OOMs on allocate)
```

Maya S: any recent model rollouts pinned to this pool? Canary?

Alex M: rolled a quantized-ggml-v2 2 hours ago, but that should reduce mem. Looking at serving logs, one job is requesting very long sequences and not closing KV caches. Suspect leak in kvcache for chat sessions.

Jamal R: quick mitigation: can we cordon gpu-2 and drain pods to other GPUs/regions? Will cause more failovers but reduces OOM noise.

Nina (oncall): notify support. I'll post initial customer advisory.

ops-bot: Runbook step 1: escalate to infra if more than 5 nodes affected. Current affected nodes: 7. Escalation required.

Alex M: executing cordon+drain on node gpu-12: `kubectl cordon gpu-12 && kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

Li: draining now, moving pods to other pools. Watch autoscaler — might oversubscribe other GPUs.

Chris P: Observing more kernel timeouts while pods restart: kernel panic traces in dmesg show `NVRM: GPU at 0000:82:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus` for some restarts. Could be driver instability under heavy allocations.

Maya S: if driver is flaky we should fallback to older driver on next maintenance window. For now, policy: route new requests away from eu-west-2a. Can we set routing-policy to prefer eu-west-2b/3?

Alex M: updated smart-routing: set region preference bias -20 for eu-west-2a for 30m. Config snippet: 
```
route_policy.update({"eu-west-2a": {"bias": -20, "duration_s": 1800}})
```

Jamal R: Also throttling incoming batch sizes for that pool: set max_batch_tokens=1024 (was 8192). Might drop throughput but prevents OOM.

Nina (oncall): Customer advisory draft: "We are investigating elevated errors and latency for generation in EU. We have routed traffic away from affected infrastructure and have temporary mitigations in place. We'll provide updates every 30 minutes." Approve?

Alex M: approve. Add note that some customers may see degraded latency if rerouted to CPU.

pagerduty: PD-84231 status: acknowledged by Alex M (oncall).

ops-bot: Auto-collector: saving diagnostics: `kubectl logs` and `nvidia-smi -q` snapshots archived to s3://redwood-ops/incident/PD-84231/diagnostics.tar.gz

Maya S: found one pod (session-svc-77) hogging KV cache: it retains 9GB of GPU memory for 20+ minute sessions. It didn't release on connection close. Repro steps attached.

Alex M: good find. Killing that pod freed up ~10GB and reduced pressure. Clearing kvcache GC in runtime: `curl -X POST http://runtime-admin.internal/clear_kvcache?pool=inference-gpu-eu-west-2a` succeeded.

Li: memory pressure dropped across pool within 60s. nvml reporting more headroom.

Chris P: but kernel driver errors persist on 2 nodes. Infra ops: can you reimage or reboot gpu nodes with kernel errors?

Infra Ops (via email->slack): queued reboots for gpu-08 and gpu-12, ETA 12 minutes. We'll monitor dmesg after reboot.

Nina (oncall): I'm preparing a customer update: "We've mitigated the root cause from a runaway KV cache and re-routed traffic. Reboots are in progress on two nodes. Please expect normal behavior to return shortly."

Jamal R: starting postmortem notes: suspected cause = KV cache leak due to session closure bug + driver frag under pressure. Immediate actions: kvcache GC endpoint, cordon/drain affected nodes, region bias, throttle batches. Follow-ups: add kvcache eviction policies, add watchdog for long-lived GPU allocations, driver health checks, automated fallback more graceful.

Alex M: handing off to next oncall (Chris P) for follow-up and validation. Handoff notes: PD-84231, mitigations applied, 2 nodes rebooting, kvcache endpoint hit, routing bias set, monitor for 30m.

Chris P: taking over. I'll confirm reboots and run validation load tests to ensure no regressions.

pagerduty: PD-84231 status: reassigned to Chris P.

incident-bot: Incident PD-84231: Update logged. Priority: P1. Next update scheduled in 30 minutes.
